## Repository files navigation

OpenVibe: an infinite canvas of real terminals for your AI coding agents

License: MIT Platform: Windows 10/11 Built with Tauri 2 Status: early preview

English · Français

OpenVibe is a desktop app that puts your AI coding agents on an infinite canvas. Each agent runs in a real terminal (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and more). You group agents into teams, brief a whole team in one line, review their changes, and hand a large task to an orchestrator that splits it, staffs it and keeps time.

Everything runs on your machine. OpenVibe adds no cloud service and no telemetry, and it never skips an agent's permission prompts. Its only request of its own is a check for updates, which you can turn off. [...] On first launch, the home screen walks you through installing an agent, adding a project and launching an agent. Something wrong? See the troubleshooting guide, or open Troubleshooting from the settings menu.

Updates. OpenVibe looks for a new release on GitHub 10 seconds after it starts, then every 6 hours, and offers to install it. Before the installer restarts it, OpenVibe saves your canvas and the terminals' history; Claude conversations can be resumed afterwards. Updates are signed: one whose signature does not match is refused. This check is the only request OpenVibe makes on its own. To turn it off, open the settings menu (the gear) and untick Rechercher les mises à jour automatiquement. [...] See SECURITY.md for the security model in more detail.

## Contributing

Bug reports, ideas and pull requests are welcome, in English or in French. Start with CONTRIBUTING.md; the ideas already in line are in BACKLOG.md. Please follow the Code of Conduct.

## License and credits

OpenVibe is released under the MIT License.

It builds on Tauri, Excalidraw, xterm.js, portable-pty and cmdk. The bundled icon libraries come from the Excalidraw community, under the MIT License; their authors are listed in `public/libraries/CREDITS.md`.

OpenVibe is an independent project. It is not affiliated with Symvibe, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google or the makers of the other agents it launches; their names belong to their owners.

results.content: Open Vibe is an open-source course and agent workflow that turns Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Open Code, or another terminal-capable AI coding agent into a SaaS-building assistant. It is built around Open SaaS, a free Wasp-powered SaaS boilerplate, so learners can create a real app while understanding the architecture behind production-ready SaaS systems. The workflow starts with setup instructions that install Node.js, install the Wasp CLI, and verify the local environment. After creating a new Wasp app, the user opens an AI coding agent inside the project and lets it fetch course module instructions. The agent then works as both tutor and pair programmer, explaining the system while helping the user build features from plain-language requests. Progress is tracked through JSON files
